1.e4 c5 2.Nc3 Nc6 3.g3 g6 4.Bg2 Bg7 5.d3.strategy: Develops the bishop towards Qd2 and long castling and takes d4 under control. The cost is that the bishop then stands where a black knight can challenge it, so White has to be ready to give up the dark-squared bishop.

The knight takes the central post and invites the e3-bishop to trade. If White trades, ...cxd4 gains time against the c3 knight and leaves Black a pawn in the centre; if White does not, the knight stays and cramps White's development.
